newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Credit rating agencies to assess Romanian economy.
newsitem.headline: Credit rating agencies to assess Romanian economy.

text.p: Three major international credit rating agencies are to evaluate the state of Romania's economy in the next few weeks, central bank (BNR) chief econimist Daniel Daianu said on Wednesday.
"Representatives of Japan Credit Rating are now in Bucharest, while Moody's and Standard and Poor's will be here in the coming days," Daianu told Reuters by telephone.
Romania rejoined world capital markets in 1995, six years after the collapse of communism.a legacy of the isolation imposed by late, megalomaniac dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
Last year, Romania was awarded a BB-plus (BB+) score by the Japan Credit Rating agency, against the BB-minus (BB-) ratings of Standard and Poors and IBCA and the Ba-three (Ba3) from Moody's.

Daianu said the agencies were unlikely to announce new assessments before the completion of talks between Romania's new centrist coalition government and international lenders such as the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

Last week the Fund started talks on the government's reform programme to resume credits suspended last year under its leftist predecessor, ousted in November elections. Talks on assistance from the World Bank and European Union are also under way.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is expected to announce the first details of the reform pledges on Thursday.
Earlier this month, the BNR said it would continue prudent borrowing policies in 1997. It is entitled by parliament to draw up to $1.6 billion and is seeking better terms for its fundraising.
Last year, the BNR drew around $1.4 billion from world markets and serviced debt payments of around $1.2 billion. Its reserves stood at $855.3 million at end-1996.
